VODOU_TOKEN: Your Vodou cloud API token from https://app.vodou.ai. Used when features need to authenticate against Vodou services (licensing, cloud sync, or account-linked behavior). Keep this secret like a password. If you are fully offline/local-only, you may leave it empty depending on what you use.
VODOU_USER_ID: Your Vodou cloud user identifier, paired with VODOU_TOKEN. Together they tell Vodou which account you are. Set both from the same place you got your token. Not your email—usually an opaque id string.
VODOU_USER_EMAIL: Your email for **local continuity / self-principal** seeding (`continuity init`, resolver). Not sent to Vodou cloud unless a feature explicitly uses it—primarily for display name and stable “you” identity in `vodou-core.db`. Optional but recommended if you want the self-principal to match your real address.
VODOU_USER_NAME: Display name paired with **VODOU_USER_EMAIL** for the seeded self-principal (e.g. how “You” appears in principals). Optional.
GH_TOKEN: A GitHub personal access token (classic or fine-grained) used when automation or MCP tools call the GitHub API (repos, PRs, issues). Create one in GitHub → Settings → Developer settings. Scope it to what you need (repo read/write, etc.).
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: API key from console.anthropic.com when you use the **Anthropic API** provider in the gateway (direct API billing). This is separate from **Claude Max / Claude CLI**, which uses the `claude` binary login instead. If you only use Claude CLI with a subscription, you often do not need this.
OPENAI_API_KEY: API key from platform.openai.com for OpenAI models (GPT-4o, o3, etc.) when OpenAI is selected as the gateway’s LLM provider. Charged per token on your OpenAI account.
OPENROUTER_API_KEY: API key from openrouter.ai when using **OpenRouter** as the LLM provider (gateway and some extraction paths). Used with OpenRouter model ids (e.g. `openai/gpt-4o`). Keep secret.
GEMINI_API_KEY: API key from Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com) for Gemini models when Google is the selected provider. Distinct from Google Cloud “API key” in some setups—use the AI Studio key the gateway expects.
GROQ_API_KEY: API key from console.groq.com. Groq hosts very fast inference for many open models; used when Groq is your provider.
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY: API key from DeepSeek’s platform when DeepSeek is your chat provider.
MISTRAL_API_KEY: API key from console.mistral.ai when Mistral is your provider.
XAI_API_KEY: API key from xAI’s console when using Grok models as your provider.
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: Token from @BotFather on Telegram (format like `123456:ABC…`). Required for the Vodou-channels Telegram bot: it is how Telegram routes messages to your bot process.
TELEGRAM_ADMIN_ID: Numeric Telegram user id (not @username) for users allowed to run admin-style bot commands. Helps lock down who can control the bot beyond normal chat.
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: Bot token starting with `xoxb-` from your Slack app (OAuth & Permissions → Install / Reinstall to Workspace after changing scopes). Used with **Socket Mode** in Vodou-channels. For **multi-member channels**, add bot scope **`users:read`** so names resolve via `users.info`; without it, senders may show as raw `U…` ids.
SLACK_APP_TOKEN: App-level token starting with `xapp-` required for Slack **Socket Mode** (websocket connection). Different from the bot token; both are usually needed for the socket bot.
SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET: Signing secret from the Slack app “Basic Information” page. Used to verify that incoming HTTP requests really came from Slack (when you use HTTP endpoints instead of or in addition to sockets).
SLACK_DEFAULT_CHANNEL: Default channel id (e.g. `C0123…`) or name used when a message does not specify a channel—so broadcasts or scripts have a sensible target.
SLACK_TOKEN: User or workspace token for the **Slack MCP** integration (search/send tools), which is separate from the Vodou-channels bot. Follow that MCP server’s docs for which token type to use.
SLACK_COOKIE: Browser cookie string some Slack MCP workflows use for authenticated browser-style access. Highly sensitive—treat like a password and rotate if leaked.
DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN: Discord bot token from the Discord Developer Portal. Powers the Vodou-channels Discord bot so it can connect to your guild and receive/send messages.
DISCORD_GUILD_ID: The numeric “server” id of your Discord guild. Used to scope bot behavior to one server and avoid acting globally by mistake.
DATABASE_TYPE: Hint for optional graph or code-graph features (e.g. `neo4j`). Only matters if you use tooling that connects to Neo4j or similar; ordinary chat and MCP do not require it.
NEO4J_URI: Bolt connection URL for Neo4j, typically `bolt://localhost:7687` or a cloud host. Used when CodeGraph or related features query a graph database.
NEO4J_USERNAME: Username Neo4j expects for authentication (often `neo4j` locally).
NEO4J_PASSWORD: Password for the Neo4j user. Stored in plain text in `.env`—protect the file.
NEO4J_DATABASE: Which Neo4j database name to use inside the server (default is often `neo4j`).
GOOGLE_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS: Absolute path to the **Google OAuth client JSON** (Desktop or Web client credentials from Google Cloud Console). Used by presets such as Google Calendar MCP—not the same as **GEMINI_API_KEY**. Keep the file outside public web roots.
OI_PROJECT_PATH: Absolute path to **this** Vodou install (folder containing `vodou-core`, `.vodou`, etc.). Installers set this so hooks, gateway, and daemons agree on the project root even if you start commands from another directory. Wrong path causes wrong DB, wrong memory, or missing `.vodou` files.
OI_MAX_PROCESSES: Maximum number of concurrent `vodou-core` child processes. The **scheduler** backs off near ~80% of this cap and the **agent** near ~60% so interactive use keeps headroom. The daemon can reap stuck processes after a timeout. Raise if you run many parallel tools; lower if the machine is small.
OI_ALLOW_HEADLESS_BRAIN: When set to `1`, the `brain` / `./oi` command is allowed to run **without a TTY** (e.g. from Cursor, Claude Code, or scripts). Default behavior may exit immediately in non-interactive contexts to avoid hangs—this overrides that so automation works.
LLM_PROVIDER: Legacy/default hint for which LLM backend to use (e.g. `claude-cli`). The **web gateway** usually prefers settings stored in its SQLite `gateway.db`, so this mainly affects CLI paths or fallbacks. Check Settings → LLM/Model for the live provider.
CLI_MODEL: Default **Claude CLI** model short name (e.g. `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`) when the gateway database does not override `cli_model`. Gateway Settings normally wins once configured.
VODOU_GATEWAY_AUTO_ENSURE: When **`0`**, **`false`**, **`no`**, or **`off`**, the gateway **does not** run `vodou-core daemon ensure` / `worker ensure` on startup or on the **60s timer** — avoids respawning daemon/worker while you replace **`vodou-core`** (macOS UE risk). Stale socket cleanup still runs. Remove or set to **`1`** after swapping the binary and restart the gateway. Alias: **`OI_GATEWAY_AUTO_ENSURE**.
VODOU_HOOK_SKIP_ENSURE: When **`1`** / **`true`** / **`yes`** / **`on`**, **`vodou-hook-bin ensure`** becomes a no-op (does not spawn the daemon). Pair with **`VODOU_GATEWAY_AUTO_ENSURE=0`** during binary swaps; rebuild **`vodou-hook-bin`** after changing hook sources. Requires the variable in the environment of the **`vodou-hook`** process (project `.env` is loaded by hooks/gateway when configured).
WEB_PORT: TCP port where **Vodou-Console** listens for HTTP/WebSocket (chat UI, REST). Default 8765. After changing, restart the gateway; anything bookmarked to the old port must be updated.
START_AIGATEWAY: When `1`, `start-vodou-services.sh` starts the Node gateway on `WEB_PORT`. When `0`, the script skips starting the web UI (you might run the gateway manually or not use it).
OI_GATEWAY_SHELL_MODE: Controls which **tools** the AI may use inside **gateway chat**: `restricted` = bash limited to vodou-core-related commands (safest on shared machines); `verify` = adds read-only file tools (Read/Grep/Glob); `full` = Claude Code–style tool parity including write/edit. Misconfiguration can expose filesystem—use `restricted` if unsure.
OI_GATEWAY_POOL_TOKEN_BUDGET: For **pooled Claude CLI** sessions: when cumulative “cache read” tokens exceed this number, the gateway **recycles** (restarts) that CLI process so the in-memory context does not grow without bound (saves cost and avoids huge prompts). Default 500000; set `0` to disable recycling (not usually recommended).
OI_GATEWAY_POOL_RESTART_ON_SYSTEM_PROMPT: When `1` or `true`, restarting or changing the **system prompt** for a pooled Claude CLI session forces a **new CLI process** instead of reusing the old one. Use if you need a clean system context after prompt tweaks; otherwise leave unset/false for fewer restarts.
OI_SMART_ROUTING: Default **on** (anything other than `0`/`false`). Sends “simple” user queries to a **cheaper/faster** model and keeps hard tasks on your primary model. Set to `0` to disable so every message uses the primary model only.
OI_SMART_ROUTING_MODEL: Override the **cheap-route** model id. Empty = automatic per provider (e.g. Haiku for Anthropic, mini models for OpenAI). Set explicitly if you want a particular small model.
OI_GATEWAY_CLI_LEGACY_ARGV_PROMPT: When `1`, the gateway passes the user message as a **legacy argv prompt** to `claude`. Default behavior uses **stdin NDJSON** (`--input-format=stream-json`) to match Claude Code. Only enable if you need old behavior for compatibility.
OI_GATEWAY_DISABLE_PERSISTENT_CLI: When `1`, disables the **persistent Claude CLI pool** and uses one-shot CLI spawns per request (slower, colder starts, but simpler lifecycle).
VODOU_GATEWAY_LIST_TOOLS_LIVE: When **`1`**, the gateway executor may run **`vodou-core list-tools`** against live MCP connections for tool lists (slower, can block). When **`0`** (default), prefer cached/registry-backed lists. Flip to **`1`** only when debugging tool registration.
OI_GATEWAY_CLI_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS: Wall-clock milliseconds allowed for **one pooled CLI turn** (one user message through tools). Default 900000 (15 minutes). Set `0` to disable the timeout (risky if a turn hangs).
OI_GATEWAY_CLI_POOL_IDLE_MS: If no work is queued for a pooled CLI session this long, the gateway **closes** it to free RAM. Default 600000 (10 minutes).
CLAUDE_MODEL: Default Anthropic **model id string** when using the API provider (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`). Gateway DB settings may override. Must match a model your key can access.
OLLAMA_BASE_URL: Base URL of your local **Ollama** server, usually `http://localhost:11434`. The gateway uses this when Ollama is the provider.
OI_CHANNEL_ATTACHMENTS_DIR: Override directory where **Vodou-channels** stores files downloaded from Slack/Telegram/Discord for vision/PDF. Default is `<OI_PROJECT_PATH>/.vodou/channel-attachments`. Use an absolute path if you want media on another disk.
WHATSAPP_AUTH_DIR: Directory for **WhatsApp** session data (Pairing/QR auth) used by Vodou-channels. Default `<OI_PROJECT_PATH>/.vodou/whatsapp-auth`. Must be persistent across restarts or you re-pair often.
CHANNEL_MEDIA_STRICT: When `1`, the gateway **rejects** attachment paths that are not under allowed roots (`CHANNEL_MEDIA_ROOTS` / defaults). Stronger security against path tricks; may block legitimate paths if misconfigured.
CHANNEL_MEDIA_ROOTS: Comma-separated list of **absolute path prefixes** the gateway may read for channel images/documents. Example: your project `.vodou` folder and `/tmp`. Anything outside these prefixes can be denied when strict mode is on.
CHANNEL_VISION_MAX_BYTES: Maximum size in **bytes** for an image (or vision payload) the gateway will accept from a channel. Prevents huge uploads from exhausting RAM.
CHANNEL_DOCUMENT_MAX_BYTES: Maximum size in bytes for **PDF or document** attachments the gateway will process.
CHANNEL_TEXT_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES: Maximum size in bytes for **plain-text** attachments.
CHANNEL_VISION_COMPAT_ENDPOINTS: Comma-separated list of **provider names** that should receive vision in a “compatible” bundled form (routing hint for multimodal). Usually leave empty unless support asked you to set it.
CHANNEL_OLLAMA_VISION: When `1` or `true`, allows a code path that sends images to **Ollama** vision-capable models. Requires Ollama and a vision model; off by default.
ORT_DYLIB_PATH: Filesystem path to the **ONNX Runtime** shared library (e.g. `onnxruntime/lib/libonnxruntime.dylib` on macOS). When set, memory can compute **vector embeddings** for hybrid search. If unset, memory may fall back to **text search only** (still useful). Older macOS versions may not support bundled ONNX—omit this to avoid load errors.
OI_MEMORY_W_VECTOR: Weight (0–1) for **vector similarity** in hybrid memory retrieval. Higher = “meaning” matters more. All weights (vector + FTS + recency + category) are normalized in code to sum to 1 for scoring.
OI_MEMORY_W_FTS: Weight for **full-text search** match quality. Higher = keyword overlap matters more in retrieved memories.
OI_MEMORY_W_RECENCY: Weight for **recency** (newer chunks score higher). Increase if you want fresher context; decrease if old but semantically relevant memories should compete equally.
OI_MEMORY_W_CATEGORY: Weight for **category** alignment between query and stored memory metadata.
OI_MEMORY_TOP_K: How many memory **chunks** to retrieve per search before ranking. Higher = broader recall but more noise and cost to send to the model.
OI_MEMORY_W_HEARTBEAT: Multiplier applied to **heartbeat-generated** memories so they do not drown out user-authored memories in search (typical default scale 0.0–1.0 style behavior—see code for exact math).
VODOU_MEMORY_RERANK_K: How many top hybrid-search candidates the **BGE cross-encoder reranker** scores (after RRF). Larger = better reordering but more CPU time. Typical **10–30**.
VODOU_MEMORY_RERANK_SKIP_COSINE: If the **best raw vector cosine** for the top RRF hit is **≥ this threshold** (0.0–1.0, default **0.75**), skip reranking—saves ~1s when the winner is already obvious. Set **`0`** to always rerank (slower).
VODOU_MEMORY_COSINE_FLOOR: Minimum **raw vector cosine** on the top memory hit for **hook / prompt injection** quality gate (daemon). Below this, results may be treated as too noisy to inject (default **0.30** in code). Tune if you get empty context or too much junk.
VODOU_MEMORY_EMBED_CPU: When **`1`**, force **CPU** path for query/chunk embeddings (disables GPU/CoreML fast path in the embedder). For debugging or comparing throughput only.
VODOU_MEMORY_RERANK_CPU: When **`1`**, force **CPU** for the reranker model. For debugging or when GPU/CoreML misbehaves.
OI_MEMORY_EXTRACTION_PROVIDER: Which backend **categorizes / extracts** memories into `memory.db` (e.g. `auto` uses your current gateway provider, or `anthropic`, `openai`, `ollama`, `claude`, `script`). Wrong value can break extraction silently—`auto` is safest if the gateway is configured.
OI_EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT_SECS: Seconds to wait for an **extraction LLM** call before failing the extraction attempt. Raise on slow networks; lower to fail fast.
OI_ENABLE_MEMORY_COMPACT_SCHEDULE: When `1`, the brain process runs a **scheduled compaction** of `MEMORY.md` (rolls up or trims per schedule). Keeps the markdown memory file from growing forever.
OI_MEMORY_COMPACT_SCHEDULE: Human-readable schedule for compaction, e.g. `every 1d`. Parsed by the in-process scheduler—see vodou-core docs for supported phrases.
OI_MEMORY_COMPACT_MAX: Safety cap: maximum number of lines or units processed **per compaction run** so one run cannot freeze the machine on a huge file.
OI_JANITOR_ENABLED: When `1`, the **worker** runs the memory **janitor** on a cron: deduplicates similar chunks, rewrites fuzzy dates to absolute ones, and prunes obsolete tagged content. Long-term memory is preserved by design; heavy deletion only triggers in edge cases (e.g. over chunk cap).
OI_JANITOR_SCHEDULE: **Cron** expression for janitor runs (default `0 2 * * *` = 02:00 daily). Uses the worker’s clock.
OI_MEMORY_CHUNK_CAP: **Emergency** ceiling on total memory chunks. A late janitor phase only engages when count exceeds this—**not** everyday pruning. Default is very high (~years of use); tune only if you understand runaway protection.
OI_JANITOR_DRY_RUN: When `1`, the janitor **never writes** to the database—reports only. Useful for auditing what it would do. Some CLI invocations also respect first-run dry-run windows.
OI_INTENT_SIGNAL_ENABLED: Master switch for the **intent signal layer** in the **daemon**: on each prompt, it can match keywords to `intent_mappings` and optionally invoke tools. Set `0` to disable the whole layer (hooks become memory-only for that path).
OI_INTENT_AUTO_ROUTE: When `0`, the daemon still **computes** intent signals and logs telemetry but **does not** call the worker/brain to inject live tool output—useful to observe matches without auto-execution.
OI_INTENT_SIGNAL_TIMEOUT_MS: Hard **timeout in milliseconds** for the worker `brain` call used during auto-routing (cold path can include spawning work). Prevents the hook from blocking your editor forever.
OI_FLUSH_EVERY_N_PROMPTS: After this many **assistant replies** in gateway chat, trigger a **memory flush** (extraction pipeline). Default 15. Lower = more frequent writes to memory; higher = fewer, larger batches.
OI_AUTONOMOUS_PLAN_PATH: Path (often under `.vodou/workspace/`) to the **autonomous plan** markdown file the scheduler’s planning step reads or updates.
OI_SCHEDULER_USE_PLANNING: When enabled, scheduler runs include an **autonomous planning** phase (ties into plan files and extraction provider). Disable for minimal scheduler behavior.
OI_SCHEDULER_MAX_RUNS_PER_DAY: Hard cap on how many **scheduler-triggered brain runs** may execute per calendar day—prevents runaway loops or API spend.
OI_SCHEDULER_TASK_TIMEOUT_SECS: Kill a **scheduled task** subprocess after this many seconds if it has not finished (stuck tool, network hang, etc.).
OI_SELF_IMPROVE_PLAN_PATH: Alternate markdown path for **self-improvement** planning content; planning code may fall back between this and `OI_AUTONOMOUS_PLAN_PATH`.
OI_WORKER_SCHEDULER_INTERVAL_SECS: How often the **worker** wakes up to check **due scheduled tasks** (seconds). Minimum enforced in code (do not set absurdly low on large installs).
OI_WORKER_SCHEDULER: Set to `0` or `false` to **disable** the worker’s periodic scheduler loop entirely (no due-task execution from DB). Heartbeat/janitor hooks inside the worker may still behave differently—restart after change.
OI_HEARTBEAT_ENABLED: When `1`, the **scheduler** triggers periodic **heartbeat** calls to your gateway: a background “think about the project” loop that can use deep thinking and tools. Disable if you want zero autonomous background LLM use.
OI_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL: Time between heartbeats, e.g. `1h`, `30m`. Parsed as a duration string by the scheduler.
OI_HEARTBEAT_MAX_TOKENS: Token budget for the **LLM portion** of one heartbeat (higher if deep thinking needs long context).
OI_HEARTBEAT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS: Maximum **tool-use rounds** per heartbeat (each round can be multiple tools). Prevents infinite tool loops.
OI_HEARTBEAT_TIER: Capability level: **0** = read-only + suggestions; **1** = may create tasks; **2** = may execute more autonomous actions. Higher tiers increase risk—keep at 0 unless you trust the loop.
OI_HEARTBEAT_ACTIVE_HOURS: Local-time window when heartbeats may run, e.g. `08:00-22:00`. Empty = **always** allowed (subject to other limits).
OI_HEARTBEAT_SUPPRESS_OK: When `1`, **HEARTBEAT_OK** status lines are **not** forwarded to external channels (Slack/Discord/etc.) so channels stay quiet.
OI_HEARTBEAT_MAX_PER_HOUR: Rate limit: maximum **heartbeat invocations per hour** to protect API quota.
OI_HEARTBEAT_MAX_FAILURES: After this many **consecutive failures** talking to the gateway, heartbeat **auto-disables** until you fix URL/auth and re-enable.
OI_HEARTBEAT_INJECT_LEDGER: When `1`, the heartbeat prompt includes your currently **open tasks** so the LLM updates them instead of regenerating duplicates each run. Default off. **Requires daemon restart** to toggle — value is cached at first scheduler tick.
OI_HEARTBEAT_AUTO_CLOSE_GREP: When `1`, each heartbeat checks `git log` (last 30 days) for commits whose messages match open task keywords. Candidates are surfaced in the prompt for LLM confirmation — the LLM marks them done with `- [x]` if the evidence is convincing. **HEAD-change gate**: the grep only runs when new commits exist since the last run (no-op if nothing changed). Default off. **Requires daemon restart** to toggle.
OI_GATEWAY_URL: Full base URL the **scheduler/worker** uses to call gateway HTTP APIs for heartbeat (e.g. `http://localhost:8765`). Must match where the gateway actually listens (scheme, host, port).
OI_GATEWAY_SCHEDULER_SECRET: Shared secret the worker sends (e.g. on heartbeat routes) so random clients cannot trigger privileged endpoints. **Must match** what the gateway expects. Empty = some routes may be open—set in production or on exposed networks.
DEBUG: Any non-empty value turns on **verbose diagnostics** in parts of the gateway (e.g. executor logging). Very noisy—use briefly while troubleshooting.
VODOU_RECALL_TRACE: If set to **any** value, **`continuity::recall`** logs one **`[continuity recall]`** line per search (principal, scope, mode, timing). Unset = off. Use briefly when debugging memory recall / Phase 2 plumbing.
OI_SHOW_RAW_RESULTS: When `1`, gateway chat shows raw **`<oi_results>`** tool blocks instead of stripping them for a cleaner UI. The gateway **re-reads** this from `.env` on some paths without a full restart.
OI_LOG_MAX_MB: When `.vodou/system.log` grows beyond this many **megabytes**, it is **rotated/trimmed** (keeps a tail). Prevents unbounded disk use.
OI_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SECS: Watchdog: **seconds** before vodou-core forcibly kills a stuck **agent/tool child** process. Raise for legitimately long tools; lower to recover faster from hangs.
OI_DISABLE_OUTPUT_PATH_INJECTION: When `1`, disables automatic **“output path” hints** appended to some tool results (used so the model knows where files landed). Enable if those hints confuse your workflow.
OI_AGENT_ENABLED: When `0` or `false`, disables the **agent layer** inside vodou-core (background agent behavior). Does not disable normal chat tools.
OI_MEMORY_ROOT: Override the directory for **workspace memory files** (default `.vodou/workspace`). Use if you keep memory on another volume or a named workspace.
OI_OPENAI_COMPAT_TOKEN: If set, HTTP requests to the gateway’s **OpenAI-compatible `/v1`** endpoints must send `Authorization: Bearer <this>`. If empty, those endpoints may be **unauthenticated**—dangerous on public networks.
OI_MCP_HEALTH_INTERVAL_MS: Milliseconds between **background MCP health checks** in the gateway (default several minutes). Shorter = fresher status, more overhead.
OI_WORKER_SOCK_FIRST_BYTE_MS: Timeout waiting for the **first byte** from the worker Unix socket when the gateway forwards a tool call—raise if the worker is cold and slow.
STACKOVERFLOW_API_KEY: API key for Stack Overflow’s API when using the **stackoverflow-mcp** integration—improves rate limits versus anonymous access.
MCP_REGISTRY_DASHBOARD_ALLOW_RUN: For the **mcp-registry** local dashboard (127.0.0.1 only): when **`1`**, allows **POST /api/run** from the UI. Off by default—prevents accidental command execution.
MCP_REGISTRY_VC_WRITE: When **`1`**, allows the MCP registry toolkit to **write** Vodou DB rows (e.g. oauth-begin probes). Legacy alias **MCP_REGISTRY_BT4_WRITE** may still be read for one release. Keep **`0`** unless you are actively using registry VC flows.
OPENAI_MODEL: Default OpenAI model id (e.g. `gpt-4o`) when OpenAI is the provider.
GOOGLE_MODEL: Default Gemini model id when Google is the provider.
GROQ_MODEL: Default Groq model id when Groq is the provider.
OLLAMA_MODEL: Model name as Ollama shows it (e.g. `llama3.2`) when Ollama is the provider.
OAUTH_DCR_CLIENT_NAME: Name shown on third-party OAuth consent screens when vodou-core registers via Dynamic Client Registration (Apps hub, oauth-begin). Default: Vodou. Override for white-label builds.
OAUTH_DCR_CLIENT_URI: Website / policy URL shown next to that name during OAuth consent. Default: https://vodou.ai. Set empty to omit client_uri in the DCR payload (only if the provider allows it).
GATEWAY_BASE_URL: Browser-visible base URL for the gateway — used as the OAuth redirect base. Must match what you register as 'Authorized redirect URIs' in Google Cloud Console (or equivalent). Not the same as OI_GATEWAY_URL (which is the internal scheduler/worker URL). Example: http://localhost:8765 or https://your-public-domain.
GATEWAY_DB_PATH: Absolute path override for gateway.db. Leave unset for default location (MCP-servers/Vodou-Console/gateway.db relative to project root). Set this when any MCP server that reads gateway tokens runs outside the standard MCP-servers/ layout.
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: Google OAuth 2.0 Client ID for the gateway's Web application client. Used by the Apps OAuth flow. Create at console.cloud.google.com → APIs & Services → Credentials.
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: Google OAuth 2.0 Client Secret — paired with GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID. Keep secret; never expose in frontend.
GITHUB_CLIENT_ID: GitHub OAuth App Client ID for the gateway's Apps flow. Create at github.com → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps.
GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET: GitHub OAuth App Client Secret — paired with GITHUB_CLIENT_ID. Keep secret.
ZAPIER_MCP_TOKEN: Zapier MCP token for the Apps flow. Generate at zapier.com/mcp (one token per Zapier account; wraps access to all your published Zaps).
DAPPIER_API_KEY: Dappier API key for AI-optimized web content retrieval. Generate at platform.dappier.com.
EXA_API_KEY: Exa Search API key for AI-native web search. Optional — free tier works anonymously; paid tiers need a key from exa.ai.
